features.title: Capability detection
features.summary: Detect terminal colors, mouse, and graphics from the environment and optional probe data.
features.whatItDoes: detectCapabilities reads environment variables and optional probe results. The function is pure. You can unit-test it without a teletypewriter (TTY). Device Attributes (DA) helpers parse probe responses. TUIX_PROBE_* environment overrides force features on or off in continuous integration (CI).
features.howToUse: Import detectCapabilities from @tuix/platform. Pass env fields such as TERM and COLORTERM. Call parsePrimaryDA when you have a Device Attributes (DA) response buffer. Set TUIX_PROBE_SIXEL, TUIX_PROBE_KITTY, TUIX_PROBE_ITERM, TUIX_PROBE_MOUSE, or TUIX_PROBE_TRUECOLOR to 0 or 1 to override detection.

features.title: Graphics encode and decode
features.summary: Encode and decode terminal images with sixel, Kitty, and iTerm2 protocols.
features.whatItDoes: encodeGraphics picks a protocol from TerminalCapabilities. It emits sixel, Kitty, or iTerm2 payloads. When no protocol fits, fallback is true. Consumers then use cell rendering. decodeGraphics reverses a known or auto-detected payload.
features.howToUse: Import encodeGraphics or the protocol helpers from @tuix/platform. Pass capabilities and image width, height, and pixel data. Check the fallback flag before you write the payload. Call writeGraphicsLive to encode and write through Live TerminalService.

features.title: Cursor Position Report
features.summary: Request and parse Cursor Position Report (CPR) replies from the terminal.
features.whatItDoes: REQUEST_CURSOR_POSITION is the Control Sequence Introducer (CSI) query for the cursor. parseCursorPositionReport reads a complete reply. accumulateCpr joins multi-chunk input until the reply is complete.
features.howToUse: Write REQUEST_CURSOR_POSITION to the terminal. Feed reply bytes into parseCursorPositionReport or accumulateCpr. Read row and column from the result when the parse succeeds.

features.title: Bracketed paste stream
features.summary: Extract pasted text from bracketed paste sequences in the input stream.
features.whatItDoes: extractBracketedPaste finds a complete paste between start and end sequences. Incomplete pastes return null so the caller can buffer. createPasteAccumulator feeds chunks and emits finished paste strings. Live InputService uses these helpers for pasteEvents.
features.howToUse: Import extractBracketedPaste or createPasteAccumulator from @tuix/core. Push input chunks into the accumulator. Handle each returned paste string as user text, not as key events.

features.title: Interactive Pseudo-Terminal
features.summary: Spawn, write, and resize an interactive Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) process.
features.whatItDoes: spawnPty starts a process under a Pseudo-Terminal (PTY) backend. The default backend wraps node-pty. PtyHandle supports write, resize, onData, onExit, and kill. createMockPtyBackend supplies an in-memory backend for unit tests.
features.howToUse: Import spawnPty from @tuix/process-manager. Pass the command, arguments, and optional size. Subscribe to onData for output. Call resize when the terminal size changes. Use createMockPtyBackend in tests without native modules.

features.title: Runtime hooks on the MVU loop
features.summary: Wire lifecycle hooks into the Model-View-Update (MVU) runtime loop.
features.whatItDoes: RuntimeHooks attach side work to init, update, render, commands, subscriptions, messages, errors, and shutdown. onMessage can return null to cancel a message. onSubscription records each subscription for observability. composeHooks merges several hook sets.
features.howToUse: Build a RuntimeHooks object with createHooks or a plain object. Pass hooks into runApp or the runtime config. Return null from onMessage to drop a message. Use composeHooks when plugins each supply their own hooks.

features.title: Render and update error recovery
features.summary: Recover from render and update errors and stop after repeated render failures.
features.whatItDoes: The Model-View-Update (MVU) runtime catches render and update failures. It calls onError with a context string. consecutiveRenderErrors counts failed paints. When the count reaches the limit, the runtime stops the loop.
features.howToUse: Provide an onError hook to log or report failures. Keep render pure so errors stay rare. Rely on the circuit breaker when paints fail in a loop. Do not disable the stop path in production apps.

features.title: JSX compile bridge
features.summary: Compile JSX into Model-View-Update (MVU) with detectInteractive, extractModel, and toView.
features.whatItDoes: detectInteractive decides if a component needs a continuous loop. extractModel builds the initial model from options, named runes, or source. extractStateFromSource reads $state and $states from source text. toView turns JSX output into a View for paint.
features.howToUse: Call compileToComponent or runApp on a JSX function. Set extractState to true for named $state fields. Override interactive when heuristics are wrong. Prefer beginModelExtraction with $state(name) for stable model keys under Bun.

features.title: Reactive runes and MVU bridge
features.summary: Use $derived, $bindable, and $states with a Model-View-Update (MVU) $set bridge.
features.whatItDoes: $derived tracks dependencies and recomputes when inputs change. runUntracked reads without tracking. $bindable supports two-way bindings. bindMvuPush routes named $set into a set UserMsg. registerKeyHandler and emitKeyToHandlers deliver keys without a raw stdin loop.
features.howToUse: Create fields with $state(init, name) or $states. Call bindMvuPush from the runtime so $set updates the model. Use beginViewHydration before paint so named runes match the model. Register key handlers once per session.

features.title: Platform LiveServices facade
features.summary: Import LiveServices and terminal helpers from one public platform package.
features.whatItDoes: @tuix/platform re-exports Live terminal, input, renderer, and storage layers. It also re-exports capability and graphics helpers. Physical Live implementations live under @tuix/core. Apps depend on the facade. Tests can supply fakes through the same service tags.
features.howToUse: Import LiveServices from @tuix/platform. Provide the layer to Effect programs that need live I/O. Import detectCapabilities and encodeGraphics from the same package. Do not import Live layers from deeper core paths in app code.
